extracted.intended_audience: aspiring essayists and general readers/contributors to a periodical (readers of The Spectator)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing/curating short, witty essays and letters for a periodical: how to handle humour, diction, contribution policy, and avoiding stylistic excesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: A jest is best delivered with a serious countenance
rubrics_metrics.description: A Jest is never uttered with a better Grace, than when it is accompanied with a serious Countenance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not telegraph the joke by a laugh or ridiculous expression beforehand — a grave manner raises expectation and preserves the surprise. Cicero's observation is cited as authority for this maxim.

rubrics_metrics.name: True humour should arise from thought and image, not mannered phraseology
rubrics_metrics.description: True Humour lies in the Thought, and arises from the Representation of Images in odd Circumstances, and uncommon Lights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on original, comical ideas and striking images rather than relying on stock 'witty' phrases. The natural beauty and force of the idea produce genuine mirth; mannered or pert phrasing tends to pall rather than heighten the effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conceal ridicule within gravity for stronger effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Ridicule is never more strong, than when it is concealed in Gravity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mask satirical or ridiculing content under a serious tone to increase its bite. Open, clownish mockery is less effective than quietly exposing folly from a sober vantage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid cant and pert phraseology (town slang) as a substitute for wit
rubrics_metrics.description: Wit and Humour are no less poorly recommended by a Levity of Phrase, and that kind of Language which may be distinguished by the Name of Cant... Our little Burlesque Authors... generally abound in these pert Phrases, which have in them more Vivacity than Wit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cant/pert phrases may give liveliness but should not replace substantive humour; beware of adopting fashionable slang or 'fantastick Habit' to appear witty — it often signals affectation rather than true wit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid pedantic, pompous expressions drawn from learned languages
rubrics_metrics.description: The Affectation of strained and pompous Expressions, fetched from the learned Languages... savours of the College.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't dress simple comedy or description in inflated, obscure classical diction. Pedantic language creates obscurity — 'every Line... is a Riddle' — and forces readers to reread rather than enjoy the humour or story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid the two extremes in humour style; aim for balance
rubrics_metrics.description: There are two Extreams in the Stile of Humour, one of which consists in the Use of that little pert Phraseology... the other in the Affectation of strained and pompous Expressions...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steer between the colloquial cant of the town and the pedantic pomp of the college; balance naturalness of thought with clarity of expression to achieve effective humour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodical editors should publish varied reader contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: I keep three Visiting-Days in the Week, I am content now and then to let my Friends put in a Word. There are several Advantages hereby accruing both to my Readers and myself... Young and modest Writers have an Opportunity of getting into Print; Again, The Town enjoys the Pleasure of Variety;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make space for letters and guest pieces to diversify content, discover new talent, supply fresh social material, and give the periodical variety with minimal editorial labour. Leaving 'commodious Spaces' between pieces can be a deliberate editorial device.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not claim merit or require respect on the basis of ancestry
rubrics_metrics.description: We can have no Merit, nor ought we to claim any Respect, because our Fathers acted well, whether we would or no.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When portraying characters or asserting authority as a writer, avoid relying on pedigree or inherited reputation as justification — merit should be grounded in present actions or qualities, not ancestral boastfulness. Satirize those who demand respect purely from lineage.
